div.head: VIII Atr 18
div.ab: And weofodþéna mæðe medemige man for Godes ege.
And weofodþéna mæðe medemige man for Godes ege.
And weofodþena mæðe medemige man for Godes ege.
Und der Rang der Altardiener werde aus Gottesfurcht gewürdigt:
And let the rank of the servants of the altar be honoured, for fear of God:
And the status of the priesthood shall be respected through the fear of God.
And the status of the ministers of the altar is to be respected for fear of God.
And the rights of the clergy who serve at the altar are to be respected for fear of God.

note.seg: Godes þeowas syndan mæðe ⁊ munde bedælde klagt Wulfstan 157; vgl. I Cn 4. 4, 3 (vielleicht hierher?) = Had 1; Polity 19. Vgl. Gl Geistliche 13a
Godes þeowas syndan mæðe ⁊ munde bedælde, laments Wulfstan 157; cf. I Cn 4. 4, 3 (perhaps relating to this passage?) = Had 1; Polity 19. Cf. Gl Geistliche 13a
nicht bloss ‘geachtet, respektiert’ (Thorpe, Schmid, Toller), sondern Cnut versteht: ‘mit Unterscheidung anerkennen’
not merely ‘respected, esteemed’ (Thorpe, Schmid, Toller); rather, Cnut understands: ‘acknowledge with discrimination’
Cf. I Cn. 4; 4, 3; Wulfstan, p. 157: Godes þeowas syndan mæðe ⁊ munde gewelhwar bedælde.

Liebermann translates weofodþéna by ‘Altardiener.’ The phrase mæsseþegnes ⁊ worldþegnes in Norðleoda laga, cap. 5, rather suggests that the idea may be ‘knight of the altar.’ In Insts. of Polity, 23, ed. Thorpe, Anc. Laws, ii. p. 336, the term is explained: weofodþen, þæt is biscop oððe mæssepreost oððe diacon.
The intervening chapters are occupied by injunctions on the payment of tithe and other dues to the Church, taken with little modification from earlier legislation.
